newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Kodak reports Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Kodak reports Q2 earnings.

text.p: Earlier, Eastman Kodak Co reported second quarter earnings per share of $1.12 a share, falling short of Wall Street analysts' forecasts. The company said its quarterly earnings were hurt by the strength of the U.S. dollar, higher marketing expenses, and higher losses for its digital products.
The following is the full text of the company's press release:

ROCHESTER, N.Y. -- July 16, 1997-- Eastman Kodak Company today reported sales of $3.853 billion for the second quarter of 1997, a decline of 6%, due to the divestiture of the marketing, service, and facilities management operations of its Office Imaging business last year. After adjusting for the divested Office Imaging business, sales increased 2%.
Net earnings for the quarter were $368 million, or $1.12 per share, a decline of 14% on a per share basis.
Earnings were adversely affected by the strength of the U.S. dollar, higher losses for digital products, continued higher marketing expenses to support the new Advantix system, and price pressures.

After adjusting for Office Imaging, sales inside the U.S. increased 2%, while sales outside the U.S. were essentially flat, including the effects of currency. Results from emerging markets generally improved during the second quarter, posting double-digit sales growth.

Sales for the first half were $6.986 billion, an increase of 2%, adjusting for Office Imaging. Net earnings were $517 million, or $1.57 per share. Excluding the charge for in-process research and development associated with the acquisition of the Wang Software business, first half earnings were $1.94 per share, 7% lower than 1996 on a per share basis.

Consumer Imaging segment sales for the second quarter were $2.121 billion, up 5%, reflecting strong growth in revenue from services, particularly photofinishing operations. Earnings from operations were $353 million during the quarter, a decline of 16% from a year ago, reflecting intensifying competitive pressures in photographic film and paper, as well as continued aggressive marketing efforts to support the Advantix system and the unfavorable effects of foreign exchange.

Sales for the Commercial Imaging segment during the second quarter were $1.739 billion, down 2% from last year (excluding Office Imaging). Earnings from operations were $197 million, down 6% from the prior year. Strong performance by Entertainment Imaging was offset by continuing weakness in the company's traditional micrographics business, as well as digital, graphic arts, and certain medical products. Both sales and earnings were negatively impacted by foreign exchange.

"We continue to be optimistic about our long-term prospects for profitable growth in both traditional and digital photographic markets," said George M.C. Fisher, Kodak's Chief Executive Officer. "However, as in the first quarter, revenue growth and profitability have fallen short of expectations. These unsatisfactory results reflect continuing problems executing some of our business plans, as well as the very significant impact of adverse foreign exchange and an intensifying competitive environment. These factors, plus the continuing heavy investment in aggressive marketing of our Advantix products and strategic investments in our digital products and services, will make it very difficult to grow 1997 operating earnings per share beyond the 1996 level."

Although losses from digital products increased during the second quarter, Fisher noted that Kodak remains committed to growing its digital portfolio in a value-creating manner, both through internal development and broader use of alliances.

"We continue to take the long view, investing for growth, particularly in Advantix, emerging markets and digital products, while managing our core consumer business both for share growth and market expansion," Fisher said. "Although we will sustain these investments, we have concluded that all company units will accelerate their on-going cost reduction programs."
"Over the long term, we remain committed to our earnings objective of an average of at least 10% earnings per share increase per year," Fisher said.

"We are encouraged by the rebound in emerging markets, the excellent consumer satisfaction levels for Advantix products, and the most competitive product portfolio we have had in years, led by our new line-up of Gold films and some highly-acclaimed new digital products," Fisher said.
"We fully expect to come out of 1997 with a stronger management team, an improved cost structure, and an advantaged position in world markets."
